article_notes: 363 Babesia smear-positive dogs from records (retrospective 2000-2009, prospective 2009-2013) at the University of Zambia clinic and two private practices in Lusaka; PCR speciation only for 62 prospective dogs (B. rossi 5, B. gibsoni 20, mixed 37). No mortality comparison is reported. Outcome groupings used: hospitalised vs outpatient; anaemia grade; PCV as continuous anaemia measure. Comparisons of rectal temperature by breed and of Table 2 haematology by species are not severity comparisons and were not extracted (except PCV, which is the anaemia measure).

severity_definitions.label: hospitalised vs outpatient
severity_definitions.definition: Dogs hospitalised (mean stay 1.74 days, up to 21 days) vs treated as outpatients. Criteria for hospitalisation not stated.
severity_definitions.quote: Of the dogs diagnosed with Babesia, 41.9% (152/363) were hospitalised, whilst the rest were treated on an outpatient basis.

severity_definitions.label: severe / moderate / mild anaemia / non-anaemic
severity_definitions.definition: PCV < 15% severe, 15-30% moderate, > 30-37% mild, > 37% non-anaemic (modified Reyers et al. 1998 / Jacobson and Tvedten and Weiss).
severity_definitions.quote: Dogs with PCV less than 15% were considered as severely anaemic, and those with PCV 15–30 as moderately anaemic, those with PCV >30–37 as mildly anaemic, and those with PCV >37% as nonanaemic.
severity_definitions.definition_source: modified Reyers et al. 1998 (cited by Jacobson) and Tvedten and Weiss

severity_definitions.label: PCV (degree of anaemia, continuous)
severity_definitions.definition: PCV (and Hb) as a continuous measure of anaemia severity, compared between factor groups by ANOVA or correlated by Pearson's r.
severity_definitions.quote: Overall mean PCV was 18.4% (±SD, range; ±9.2, 5.0–49.0) and overall mean Hb was 6.4 g/L (±SD, range; ±3.04, 1–14.1).

associations.species: mixed (B. rossi, B. gibsoni and mixed infections)
associations.statistic: ANOVA F 1, 362 = 5.25; hospitalised mean PCV ± SD = 15.36 ± 6.18, outpatient 21.36 ± 7.60
associations.quote: There was no significant difference in the proportion of anaemia and PCV in dogs that were hospitalised and those that were not (ANOVA: F 1, 362 = 5.25; P = 0.030; hospitalised mean PCV ± SD = 15.36 ± 6.18, outpatient mean PCV ± SD = 21.36 ± 7.60).
associations.note: Checker flags 362: it is the ANOVA degrees of freedom printed as F 1, 362 (comma read as decimal). Text says no significant difference, but the printed P = 0.030 is below the stated alpha (P <= 0.05): set unclear. The proportion of anaemia was also said not to differ, with no numbers.

associations.species: mixed (B. rossi, B. gibsoni and mixed infections)
associations.statistic: Chi-square χ2 = 5.636, df = 1; 6 of 7 transfusions in hospitalised dogs
associations.quote: Hospitalised dogs were more likely to be the ones given a blood transfusion than outpatient cases (χ ^2 = 5.636, df = 1, and P = 0.018)
associations.note: Transfusion is itself a marker of treatment intensity (close to the definition). Outpatient group had only one transfusion; authors note the chi-square assumption is violated.

associations.species: mixed (B. rossi, B. gibsoni and mixed infections)
associations.quote: There were also no differences in proportions of dogs showing severe anaemia by age class (Figure 3).
associations.note: Test (presumably chi-square) and per-age values not given in text (Figure 3 only). Only dogs aged 3 months to 2 years included non-anaemic dogs.

associations.marker_as_reported: Babesia species (single B. rossi vs single B. gibsoni vs mixed infection)
associations.species: B. rossi, B. gibsoni (Asian genotype) and mixed
associations.statistic: ANOVA F 2, 60 = 2.03; mean PCV ± SD: B. rossi 10.67 ± 1.53, B. gibsoni 16.11 ± 6.81, mixed 20.15 ± 9.94
associations.quote: but the differences were not significant (ANOVA: F 2, 60 = 2.03; P = 0.15; B. rossi mean PCV ± SD 10.67 ± 1.53; B. gibsoni mean PCV ± SD 16.11 ± 6.81; mixed infection PCV ± SD 20.15 ± 9.94)
associations.note: Three species groups: severe_value = single B. rossi (n=5, lowest PCV), comparison_value = mixed infection (n=37); single B. gibsoni (n=20) intermediate. Direction 'mixed' because the factor is categorical with three levels (single infections had lower PCV and Hb than mixed). Hb by species in Table 2 (4.07, 5.26, 6.86 g/dL), described as not significant.

associations.marker_as_reported: breed (mongrel vs exotic breeds and crosses)
associations.species: mixed (B. rossi, B. gibsoni and mixed infections)
associations.statistic: ANOVA F 1, 362 = 0.02; exotic mean PCV ± SD 18.28 ± 8.94, mongrel 18.5 ± 9.62
associations.quote: There were no statistical differences in PCV between mongrels and exotic breeds and their crosses (ANOVA: F 1, 362 = 0.02; P = 0.876; exotic mean PCV ± SD 18.28 ± 8.94, mongrel mean PCV ± SD 18.5 ± 9.62).
associations.note: Checker flags 362: ANOVA degrees of freedom printed as F 1, 362. No severe/comparison group: exotic 18.28 ± 8.94 vs mongrel 18.5 ± 9.62.

associations.species: mixed (B. rossi, B. gibsoni and mixed infections)
associations.statistic: Pearson r = 0.231 between PCV and rectal temperature
associations.quote: There was a weak positive significant correlation between PCV and rectal body temperature (r = 0.231, P = 0.017).
associations.note: Positive correlation of temperature with PCV means lower temperature goes with more severe anaemia, hence negative_association with severity. Number of dogs in the correlation not stated.
